page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture running at 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core testing. Memory performance is also a highlight, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier, supported by a cached read-only memory bandwidth of 527.19 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and complex cryptographic workloads show moderate results, with the PassMark CPU score and encryption tests falling into the lower percentiles.

Given its balanced resource allocation and strong single-core efficiency, the m9g.xlarge is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded compute, large-scale LLM inference, or cryptographic-heavy tasks due to lower multi-core scaling and weak encryption benchmark scores. The ARM64 architecture offers a highly resource-efficient profile for organizations looking to optimize compute density without the overhead of x86-based hardware.
